title: Grateful Dead Live at Seattle Center Arena on 1973-06-26
source: Teddy edited all original aud shnid "12076" with silence removal, heavy hiss reduction, eq'ing and retracking in late 11/2006.

ai_review.summary: Smooth soundboard recording (with minimal audience patches) captures a high‑energy 1973 show featuring a smoking Jack Straw, inventive Other One → Bobby McGee jam and a superb Playin' in the Band.
ai_review.review: The SBD source is generally crisp with excellent stereo separation and a punchy kick drum, though a few splice glitches and a slightly tinny audience patch are noted. Musically the band is at the height of its powers – Jerry “smokes,” Phil “kills it” on PITB, Keith’s Rhodes shines, and the set flows effortlessly from Jack Straw through Here Comes Sunshine into an inspired Other One/Bobby McGee sequence.

ai_rating.rationale: All three reviewers are enthusiastic (4‑5 stars), highlighting both a strong performance and high‑quality soundboard audio; detailed comments give confidence in the rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Exceptional fidelity with nice even mix and strong stereo; occasional splice/skip in Bertha and a slightly tinny audience patch, missing Black Peter board segment, some digital hiss reduction applied.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Smooth transitions (e.g., China Cat → Rider, Truckin' → The Other One) keep the momentum high; audience patches fill missing board parts without breaking flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as “smoking,” turned up loud on several songs, and providing strong harmonies throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: “Kills it” during Playin' in the Band, huge presence in the mix, picks up slack when other parts dip, excellent bass work noted.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals praised – “Bobby nails the vocals,” with tight rhythm guitar support.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s Rhodes highlighted (splattering on walls, perfect on He's Gone), though briefly buried during some jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Kick drum noted for extra ‘umph’; overall drum work solid and supportive.
